subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Telegraph: Wiring the World
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Telegraph: Wiring the World.

hook.text: In 1830, a message from New York to London took 3 weeks by ship. By 1866, it took seconds.

buildup.text: Samuel Morse used electrical pulses through wire. Short and long pulses formed a code — dots and dashes.

discovery.text: The first transatlantic cable failed after 3 weeks. The insulation dissolved in saltwater.

twist.text: The second cable, laid by Brunel's Great Eastern in 1866, worked. It changed commerce overnight.

climax.text: By 1880, 100,000 miles of undersea cable connected every continent. The internet has ancestors.

punchline.text: The internet started with dots and dashes.

quiz.question: Why did the first transatlantic telegraph cable fail?
options: Lightning strikes destroyed the sending equipment
The insulation dissolved in saltwater after three weeks
A ship anchor cut through the cable on the ocean floor
